clue.text: Bill, grabbed by impertinent girl, leaving coat on road?

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside the grabber, so the bill's letters go into the girl's

parts.note: a cheeky, forward young woman is called a madam
AC is short for account, which a bill is

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl snatches the bill and walks off, abandoning her coat in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like clothing, but the definition is a surface layer laid on a road; the question mark flags that sideways reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmacadam is a surfacing of broken stone spread over a roadway, literally a coating for it.

clue.text: After a short time wine makes one anything but cheerful

indicators.note: the wine's letters come after those of the short time, giving the order of the pieces

parts.note: MO is short for moment, as in 'wait a mo'
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A quick drink of wine is supposed to cheer you, yet it leaves one gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sullen and gloomy is the opposite of cheerful, so the phrase is a synonym by negation.

clue.text: Loveless individual in army bashed on the head

indicators.note: the shortened individual sits inside the army's letters

parts.note: an army can mean a large crowd, as in an army of fans

indicators.note: love is O in tennis scoring, so loveless means the O is dropped

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A lonely soldier in the ranks gets hit over the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, hence O; 'Loveless' drops it. 'army' here means any large throng of people, not soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to crown someone is to hit them on the top of the skull.

clue.text: Distress of female in US university after party

indicators.note: the university piece follows the party piece in the answer

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: the female's letter is placed within the university's letters

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A woman at an American college is upset after a night out partying.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit is to upset or unsettle, and the noun likewise means unease or embarrassment, close to distress.

clue.text: Islamic ruler's beginning to sink in boggy ground

indicators.note: the ruler's first letter sinks down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A Muslim potentate starts to go under in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of EMIR, E, drops from the top to the foot of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mire is swampy, muddy land such as a bog, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Glib accounts one ignored following travel books

indicators.note: the trimmed accounts come after the travel word

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: the one is left out of the accounts

parts.note: spiels are smooth, glib patter or sales talk
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Slick travel stories in guidebooks, with one left unread.
explanation.definitionFit: The four Gospels are the New Testament books of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

clue.text: Female in uniform given old-fashioned punishment for making suggestions

parts.note: a Guide is a member of the uniformed Girl Guides
lines were sentences a pupil had to copy out repeatedly as a school punishment

explanation.surface: A uniformed girl is given a traditional school punishment for offering advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl Guides are the British equivalent of Girl Scouts; 'lines' was the old school penalty of writing a sentence out many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidelines are recommendations or advice on how to act, a synonym of suggestions.

clue.text: Loudmouth putting men off the tube

indicators.note: the men are taken off the end of the loudmouth

parts.note: a stentor is a person with a very loud voice, after the Greek herald in the Iliad
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A noisy passenger shoves the other men off the Underground train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tube' suggests London's Underground, but the definition is a small medical tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A stent is a small mesh tube inserted into a vessel to hold it open.

clue.text: Property returned in the case getting knocked about

indicators.note: being battered out of shape signals that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something given back in its box, which has been bashed in transit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting knocked about' rearranges THE CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, escheat is land that reverts to the Crown or state when the owner dies without heirs.

clue.text: Thus heartless boss, political type, makes attempt to arouse sympathy

parts.note: so means thus, in that way

indicators.note: the middle letters of the boss are removed, leaving only the ends

parts.note: taken as written before its centre goes
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted Conservative boss tries to win pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips OS from the middle of BOSS, leaving BS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tale of hardship told to make people feel sorry for the teller.

clue.text: Provision of refreshments that would suit a small congregation?

definitions.text: Provision of refreshments that would suit a small congregation?

parts.words: Provision of refreshments that would suit a small congregation?
parts.note: a hotel's in-room meal delivery, read as a church service small enough to hold in one room

explanation.surface: Which catering arrangement best serves a tiny church gathering?
explanation.walkthrough: The hotel term for bringing food to guests' rooms is reread as a religious service held in a single room.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels deliver food and drink to guests' rooms; a small congregation could equally worship in a room.

clue.text: Simple dwelling lacking home for vehicle

indicators.note: the home is missing from the simple dwelling

parts.note: a cabin is a basic hut
in means at home

explanation.surface: A homeless person's rough shelter is a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a taxi, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Deity to be celebrated with event coming round

parts.note: to be sung is to be celebrated in song

indicators.note: turning round means the event's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or event

explanation.surface: A god honoured at a festival that comes round each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Ra or Helios, a god of the sun, is a specific kind of deity.

clue.text: Most considerate, giving information before learner enters exam

indicators.note: the information comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the learner goes inside the exam

parts.note: a test is an exam
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: The kindest examiner briefs the learner driver before the test begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentlest is the superlative of gentle, meaning kindest and most thoughtful.

clue.text: A bishop has way of speaking about a regrettable royal event?

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: the way of speaking goes around the second a

parts.note: diction is one's manner of enunciation

explanation.surface: A bishop's speech concerns an unfortunate episode for the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward VIII gave up the throne in 1936; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A king giving up his throne, as Edward VIII did, is a royal occasion many regret.

clue.text: A bolder flirt, one plays around — it can be shocking

indicators.note: fooling about signals these letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A brazen flirt fools around, and that is scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays around' rearranges A BOLDER FLIRT together with I. 'shocking' looks like scandal but means an electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: This machine delivers an electric jolt to restart a heart, so it literally gives shocks.

clue.text: A bit of fun with footballers appearing in bloomers

parts.note: a lark is a prank or bit of fun
Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club

explanation.surface: Footballers mess about in baggy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests old-fashioned knickers, but means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspurs are flowering garden plants, so they are things that bloom.

clue.text: Hindu god outside prison set up somewhere in India

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the letters read from bottom to top
the god's letters go around the prison

parts.note: Rama is a Hindu god, an avatar of Vishnu
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity standing outside a jail somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the god round the prison, and 'set up' then reads the whole of that bottom to top, as suits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in Punjab, home of the Golden Temple, so it is a place in India.

clue.text: One ruined team, after transformation, went to great heights?

indicators.note: once changed in form, these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A failing side, once overhauled, rose to great success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after transformation' rearranges ONE RUINED TEAM. 'went to great heights' sounds like success, but is literal climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To mountaineer is to climb mountains, literally going up to lofty altitudes.

clue.text: Lots of superior chaps keeping private

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially superior

indicators.note: the chaps hold the private within them

parts.note: men are chaps
PTE is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

explanation.surface: Many upper-class men are holding a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a great many, an indefinite large number.

clue.text: Something to make small hole, allowing river to enter in trickle

indicators.note: the river goes inside the hole-making tool

parts.note: a dibble is a pointed gardening tool for making holes for seeds

explanation.surface: Bore a small hole and let the river seep in slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dribble is to flow in a thin, slow stream, the same as a trickle.

clue.text: Holy woman with little time for wine

parts.note: St Clare of Assisi, founder of the Poor Clares
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A nun with a spare moment has a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Commanding little devil, last in the den, retreating

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word the is taken
going backwards means the den's letters are reversed

parts.note: a lair is a den

explanation.surface: An imperious little devil withdraws last of all into its den.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means majestic and authoritative, like an emperor's bearing.

clue.text: Copy, somewhat inferior perhaps, on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror image runs backwards, so the letters read in reverse
only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: A reproduction that, thinking it over, may be second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ORPER sits inside 'inferiOR PERhaps'; 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy of an original work or piece of furniture.

clue.text: Failure, I admitted in retrospect, making observation

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read backwards
the failure lets the I in

parts.note: a lapse is a failure or slip

explanation.surface: Looking back, I confessed my mistake, which was a fair remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts I inside LAPSE to make LAIPSE, which 'in retrospect' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an archaic word for spying or watching, the act of observing.

clue.text: Capital to suffer 1666 event as reported

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so we hear a word that sounds the same

parts.note: London's Great Fire was in 1666, so to undergo it is to burn

explanation.surface: A city destined to go through a disaster like that of 1666, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Fire of London destroyed much of the City in 1666.
explanation.definitionFit: Bern is the seat of the Swiss government, the federal capital of Switzerland.

clue.text: Maiden rejected by flood survivor — the one demanding obedience?

indicators.note: the maiden is cast out of the survivor's name

parts.note: Shem, a son of Noah, survived the Flood in the ark
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl spurned by a survivor of the Flood, by the woman who insists on being obeyed.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard's novel 'She' features Ayesha, 'She-who-must-be-obeyed', a phrase Rumpole used for his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard's immortal queen is known as She-who-must-be-obeyed, a woman insisting on obedience.

clue.text: Proper identification for additive in 2017?

parts.note: prim means primly correct, proper
an E-number is the EU code identifying a food additive

explanation.surface: The correct code label for a food additive in a particular year.
explanation.walkthrough: 2017 looks like a year, but it is an example of the definition, as the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: 2017 has no divisors but one and itself, so it is an example of this arithmetic class.

clue.text: Town has to manage growth — that's hard

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
a corn is a hard thickened growth of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A town struggles to control its expansion, which is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Runcorn is a town in Cheshire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is an industrial town in Cheshire, England, an example of a town.

clue.text: It'll be easy, not as we planned

indicators.note: arranged according to a plan, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says a job will be simple, though things did not go as intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges NOT AS WE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'no problem', a reassurance that a task will be simple.
